_what_this_is: A push policy: an insurance-shaped budget on what an agent may push to git. Mandate-shaped (doctrine 07): issuer, subject, scope, interval. The pool is shared by every agent pushing to this repository, because the ledger lives in the repository.
_authority: This document is the policy. check.py computes a verdict from it and the ledger, and never from anything else. Numbers are the project lead's from memo 12 and are placeholders until the ledger has enough entries to re-fit them (doctrine 12 §5).
_mode: refuse (the default): check.py exits 1 on a refusal and the push stops · notify: the same verdict is computed and recorded, and the push proceeds. Set to notify by the project lead on 5 September 2026 ('for now you can relax this rules as just for notification'); to be reviewed with the limits. Every ledger entry records the mode it was produced under.
subject: any agent pushing to this repository

own.note: the agent's own branch. Memo 12 says 'five times a day, or ten' and 'a bucket of 20 or 50'; the larger normal and the smaller pool are taken, so the buffer is 2x normal

dev.note: memo 12: 'push to the dev branch three times a day' and 'maybe 10 for the dev branch'

bytes.unit: bytes of new objects per push, uncompressed, measured by git before the push (a floor: wire bytes after packing are smaller)
bytes.note: memo 12: 50k normal, 'no commit should be more than 300k', 'a megabyte of budget'. The project lead's earlier message said 250k for the per-push maximum; the memo's 300k is used and the difference recorded

verdicts.normal: within the normal band; nothing drawn
verdicts.drawn: over the normal band, within the per-occurrence limit, pool had enough: the excess is DRAWN from the pool (a claim, paid in the resource, doctrine 12 §1)
verdicts.refused: over the per-occurrence limit, or the pool cannot cover the excess: the push is refused and the agent must stop

does_not_prove: That these numbers fit this repository. They are the memo's, and the backtest in README.md shows what they would have said about the estate's own recent pushes.

That the check is a boundary. The ledger is in the repository and the check runs where the agent runs, so an agent can edit both: this is a SETTING (doctrine 05). A boundary is the same check run by a party the agent cannot reach, such as a required CI check.
That bytes measured before the push equal bytes on the wire. git packs and compresses; this counts uncompressed new objects, which is the floor the estate's grant rule prefers.

_revisions.what: bands ×4 (50 KB → 200 KB normal per push), the per-push maximum 300 KB → 1 MB (the vendor's recommended maximum file size), the daily pool 1 MB → 4 MB, pushes own 10/20 → 20/40, dev 3/10 → 5/10
_revisions.why: 'I accept the exhaustion and can you also increase those limits for now, since they are clearly too low for this session (we will review their use and correct values later)'. The ledger's first day: one pack's publication drew the whole pool; a one-line change to a large generator costs the whole file; a release of this site weighs 250–300 KB. The first re-fit from the loss data (GM-D101); to be reviewed

_revisions.what: mode: notify — every verdict is computed and recorded exactly as before, and a refusal no longer stops the push (check.py exits 0; the entry carries mode=notify)
_revisions.why: 'Yes please push, accept these changes (also for now you can relax this rules as just for notification)'. The v0.1.69 release was the fourth in a row to cross the per-push maximum (1,169,648 B to the branch, 1,205,461 B to dev, against 1,048,576 B), each time because a one-line change to a generated file weighs the whole file. The refusal and the acceptance are both on the ledger; the numbers still count what would have been refused. To be reviewed with the limits
